name: adbc_scanner
description: ADBC (Arrow Database Connectivity) is a standard API for database drivers that exchange data in Apache Arrow format. ADBC Scanner connects DuckDB to databases through these drivers, so you can query remote data and join it with local tables.

cta.title: Talk to Any ADBC-Speaking Database
cta.description: Query, write, and inspect external databases through their ADBC drivers, with Arrow batches at the DuckDB interface.

quickStart.title: Query an in-memory SQLite database
quickStart.description: Attach SQLite through its ADBC driver and query a constant with an explicit result schema.
quickStart.note: A successful query returns one row with `id = 1`. If your installed extension still uses `adbc_connect`, [update it](#install-the-driver-and-extension) before running this example.
quickStart.requirements: Install the SQLite driver with `dbc install sqlite` before running the SQL. The [setup instructions](#install-the-driver-and-extension) cover installing dbc and updating the extension. This example uses DuckDB 1.5.6 and ADBC Scanner build `9723c3c` from the community repository.

introduction.title: Connect through a database driver
paragraphs: An ADBC driver handles the connection to a particular database, such as SQLite, PostgreSQL, or a Flight SQL service. ADBC Scanner loads that driver into DuckDB and exposes the connection through ATTACH. You can browse remote tables, send SQL to the remote database, and join the results with local data.

Use it when an ADBC driver is available for your source. The driver supplies results in Arrow batches; its network protocol and supported operations depend on the database. Install the driver separately from this extension. The SQLite example below shows both parts of that setup.
